name: DrAnmar Hemostasis Vessel and Clip
purpose: An independent hollow vessel and one-piece vascular clip asset for pressure-diameter response, manipulation, clip placement, occlusion, retention, leakage and failure research.

wall_layers.role: inner blood-contacting layer and lumen surface
smooth-muscle and elastin-dominant compliant middle layer

stable_physx_proxy.backend_limitation: current PhysX volume deformable uses one material per body
stable_physx_proxy.promotion_boundary: explicit anisotropic per-wall-layer mechanics require a qualified per-element material backend

gaps.risk: diameter, wall thickness, branch geometry, disease, age and preparation vary strongly by vessel and patient
gaps.mitigation: fit hierarchical geometry and material distributions by vessel class, pathology and preparation state

gaps.risk: the stable lane cannot reproduce full layer-specific anisotropy, viscoelasticity, active tone and collagen recruitment
gaps.mitigation: retain layer IDs and qualify nonlinear solvers against pressure-diameter, axial and cyclic tests

gaps.risk: opening angle, axial prestretch and surrounding-tissue support change vessel response
gaps.mitigation: measure unloaded geometry, opening angle and in-situ axial stretch before parameter fitting

gaps.risk: a rigid proxy cannot reproduce one-piece clip bending, yield, work hardening and springback
gaps.mitigation: promote closure only after a rod or MPM plasticity model matches force-gap and residual-shape curves

gaps.risk: wet friction, jaw alignment, vessel angle and local wall folding govern slip and sealing
gaps.mitigation: calibrate synchronized clip pose, jaw force, wall deformation, slip and leakage across conditions

gaps.risk: lumen appearance alone does not prove a pressure-tight seal
gaps.mitigation: require pressure-ramp leakage tests and retained occlusion after unloading

gaps.risk: static geometry omits pulsatile fluid-structure interaction, viscosity variation and pressure transients
gaps.mitigation: couple a qualified CFD or reduced-order lumen model and conserve fluid mass

gaps.risk: excess closing force can crush, cut through or rupture a vessel without a visible early cue
gaps.mitigation: fit element-level damage and failure from histology-linked compression, pull and burst tests

gaps.risk: specularity, blood, smoke, compression and camera exposure obscure vessel and clip state
gaps.mitigation: validate vessel, clip, lumen and leak perception on held-out synchronized endoscopic data

gaps.risk: mesh density, contact margins, time step and solver iterations affect closure, slip and pressure results
gaps.mitigation: require mesh and time-step convergence below five percent for every promoted metric

requirements.evidence: positive tetrahedral volume, one watertight hollow wall, open lumen, complete layer partition and deterministic hashes
native finite-state, inversion, pressure-diameter, volume and replay sweeps
force-gap, yield, unloading springback and residual shape agreement
retained lumen-area reduction and leak rate through the proof-pressure ramp
axial and oblique dislodgement force distributions across vessel diameter, wetness and closure state
wall crush, cut-through, rupture and burst envelopes under held-out conditions
independent clinical validation for the intended use

evidence.title: Isaac for Healthcare asset catalog v0.7.0
evidence.used_for: confirmed static anatomy vessel geometry and absence of an interactive vessel, clip, occlusion or leakage asset

evidence.title: Mechanical characterization of blood vessels and substitutes
evidence.used_for: nonlinear anisotropic viscoelastic compliance, wall dimensions, pressure-diameter behavior and burst testing

evidence.title: Mechanical properties and compositions of native arteries
evidence.used_for: pressure-diameter compliance, failure stress and burst-pressure measurement

evidence.title: Safety evaluation of laparoscopically applied clips
evidence.used_for: clip dislodgement direction, vessel diameter dependence and leakage qualification

evidence.title: Resistance of vessel occlusion methods to hydrostatic pressure
evidence.used_for: pressure-ramp leak testing and clip occlusion proof-pressure evidence

evidence.title: Vascular mechanobiology functional requirements
evidence.used_for: compliance, burst pressure, wall thickness and diameter as coupled validation targets
